response.why: batch: player A starts

3 Mountains (solid mana) + 2 castable 1/1s (Kird Ape turn 1, another turn 2). Meets the keep threshold: 2+ lands, 1-2 early plays. Weak without Forests, but playable for mono-red aggro; mulligan to 6 is not worth it here.
Turn 1 precombat main: I haven't played a land yet, so I MUST play a Mountain first (skipped land drops are permanent losses). Then I'll have a red mana open to cast a creature.

Turn 1: cast Kird Ape to start building pressure. Shock has no immediate target yet and is better saved for removal or face damage later. Aggro needs creatures in play attacking, not reactive spells on turn 1.

Upkeep on turn 3: no upkeep triggers for me. Pass to draw step, then I'll have full information and mana to cast spells in main phase. Casting Monstrous Rage or Shock now (before drawing) wastes resources—better to draw first, play land, and sequence optimally.

Leaf 0 (no attack): passive, gives opponent time to stabilize with creatures next turn. Leaf 1 (attack): establishes clock/pressure with 1 damage, races them down. Opponent has no creatures yet, so tapping my Ape is safe now. Even if they remove it with Go for the Throat, it's a fair 1-for-1 trade. Aggro wins by racing; attacking is correct.

After declaring attackers, I'm in a priority window before blockers. My Kird Ape is unblocked (opponent has no creatures), so no need to pump it. Shock and Monstrous Rage are better held for removal or postcombat plays. Pass, let combat damage resolve (1 damage to face), then move to postcombat main.

Declare blockers phase: opponent has no creatures, so they cannot block. I have no need to cast tricks here—pass priority, let them pass (no blockers available), move to combat damage, Kird Ape deals 1 damage (20→19 life), end combat.

Combat damage phase: opponent took 1 damage (20→19). No instants are useful here (opponent has no creatures to target, and face damage is better held for later or end-of-game reach). Pass priority, end combat, move to postcombat main phase where I can cast creatures.
End combat phase: no effects or actions needed here. Pass to enter postcombat main phase where I can play my second land and cast the second Kird Ape to build pressure.

Postcombat main: play my second Mountain (I can now cast 2 spells with 2 red mana instead of 1). Then I'll cast Kird Ape to add pressure—double attackers next turn is strong against an opponent with no board yet. Establishing a growing clock wins races.

Cast Kird Ape with 1 red mana (I have 2 available). This adds a second creature to attack next turn. Then I'll cast Shock with my remaining red mana for face damage, accelerating my clock. Building pressure is the aggro plan.

Cast Shock (1 red) for 2 damage to opponent's face. I have 1 untapped Mountain available after casting Kird Ape. This accelerates my clock: opponent at 17 life. Next turn I attack with 2 Kird Apes for 2 more damage. Monstrous Rage is better held for combat tricks.

Target player B (opponent at 19 life). Shock deals 2 damage for reach. Opponent drops to 17 life. I'm racing with my creatures attacking next turn, so face damage accelerates my clock. Never target my own creatures unless necessary for removal/survival.

Upkeep: no upkeep effects for me. Pass to draw step. Opponent has 2 Forests (no creatures yet—unusual for Dimir). I have 2 untapped Kird Apes ready to attack. Planning to attack hard next turn if they don't play blockers.

Leaf 0 (no attack): passive, gives opponent time to play creatures and stabilize—score 40. Leaf 1 (attack-all): deal 2 damage/turn, racing hard. Opponent at 17 life, no blockers. With Lightning Bolt (3), Shock (2), Monstrous Rage in hand, I can handle threats with burn—score 75. Leaves 2&3 (hold one Kird Ape): 1 damage/turn is too slow a clock, only benefit is one blocker—score 52. Attack all wins races; opponent has no creatures yet.

Declare attackers phase: my 2 Kird Apes are attacking. Opponent has no creatures and no blockers available. Pass priority, let combat damage resolve (2 damage to opponent: 17 → 15 life), move to end of combat.
Declare blockers phase: opponent has no creatures to block with. Pass priority. They'll pass (no blocks available), move to combat damage where my 2 Kird Apes deal 2 damage unblocked (15 life).
Combat damage phase: 2 unblocked Kird Apes deal 2 damage to opponent (15 → 13 life). No instants needed. Pass priority, let damage resolve.
End combat phase: no effects trigger. Pass to postcombat main, where I can play my remaining land and cast Shock or Lightning Bolt for reach damage.
Opponent's turn 6 upkeep. I have no responses. Pass priority and yield to my next turn—I'll reassess once they've played and attacked (or chosen not to).

Turn 7 precombat main: play Mountain (land drop). Opponent has 2 Forests, 15 life, graveyard has Redwood Treefolk (removed somehow). I'll then have 3 untapped Mountains for mana, can cast burn or hold for combat tricks. Establish mana before committing to spells.

Cast Lightning Bolt (1 red, 3 damage to opponent's face). Opponent at 15 life, no creatures. I have 3 Mountains for mana. Deal face damage early, then cast Shock next for 2 more (total 5), then attack with 2 Kird Apes. Reach damage accelerates my clock.
Target opponent's life total (player B at 15). Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage → opponent to 12. Face damage wins races; dealing reach damage now accelerates my clock.
Cast Shock (1 red, 2 damage to opponent). Opponent at 12 life → 10 life. Still have 1 untapped Mountain for future play. Dealing reach damage continues the aggressive plan before combat.
Target opponent's life (player B at 15). Shock deals 2 damage → opponent to 13. Continue face damage before combat to establish pressure.

Pass and move to combat. Hold Monstrous Rage as a combat trick—cast it after blockers are declared to pump the creature actually in a fight. Moving to combat to attack with 2 Kird Apes and establish pressure.

Opponent at 10 life, critically low. Leaf 0 (no attack): passive, lets opponent stabilize—score 35. Leaf 1 (attack-all): 2 damage → 8 life, closes the game fast. With burn in hand and Monstrous Rage for threats, tapping both creatures is acceptable when opponent is so close to death—score 70. Leaves 2-3 (hold): 1 damage slower, but preserve blockers—score 50 each. Attack-all wins the race decisively.

Declare attackers phase: my 2 Kird Apes are attacking unblocked. Pass priority—opponent has no blockers (no creatures), so the pump doesn't increase unblocked damage this turn. Save mana for future plays (hold Monstrous Rage for when it provides actual combat advantage or hold it for later turns). Let combat resolve.

Declare blockers phase (opponent's decision): they have no creatures to block with (only 2 Forests in play). Pass priority, they'll pass with no blocks, move to combat damage where my 2 Kird Apes deal 2 damage unblocked (opponent: 10 → 8 life).

Combat Damage phase: Pass priority. Opponent has no blockers; 2 Kird Apes deal 2 unblocked damage (opponent: 8 → 6 life). No reason to pump with Monstrous Rage or tap additional mana. Proceed to damage resolution and end of combat.

End Combat phase: Pass priority. No reason to pump my creatures or tap for mana. Creatures will untap naturally. Move to Main Phase 2 where I can play the Mountain from my hand and potentially cast Monstrous Rage if needed.

Postcombat Main phase: Pass priority. No value in casting Monstrous Rage now—the pump effect ends immediately after my turn, and I can't attack again this turn. Opponent at 8 life; my Kird Apes will attack again next turn. Preserve Monstrous Rage for later if needed.
End Turn phase: Pass priority. Cleanup phase—no actions available. End my turn and move to opponent's turn 8. My Kird Apes will untap at the start of my next turn.
Opponent's upkeep (turn 8): Pass priority. No instants to cast, no responses needed. Let opponent's turn proceed. My creatures remain active for my next turn's attack.

Precombat Main phase (turn 9): Play Mountain. This is my land drop for the turn. After playing the land, I'll have 4 Mountains available to cast Searing Spear (costs 1R, dealing 3 damage) before attacking with my Kird Apes. This puts opponent from 8 life → 5 life → 3 life after combat.

Cast Searing Spear (1R, instant). Deals 3 damage to opponent (8 → 5 life). I have 4 untapped Mountains to pay the cost. After combat with 2 Kird Apes, opponent drops to 3 life. One more turn of attacks should close out the game.
Target opponent player B. Searing Spear deals 3 damage directly (8 → 5 life). Opponent is the only relevant target here—attacking them is the path to victory.

Pass priority. I've cast Searing Spear (3 damage dealt, opponent: 8 → 5 life). Move to combat phase to attack with 2 Kird Apes (2 more damage, opponent: 5 → 3 life). No reason to cast Monstrous Rage now—save it for strategic use or let combat finish the plan.
Pass priority again to end Precombat Main phase. Move to combat phase to attack with 2 Kird Apes for 2 damage (opponent: 5 → 3 life). Game should end soon as opponent has few options remaining.
Begin Combat phase: Pass priority. Move to Declare Attackers step where I'll attack with both Kird Apes for 2 total damage (opponent: 5 → 3 life).

Leaf 0 (attack-none): Score 5—passive play wastes tempo with opponent at 5 life; gives them another turn to draw threats. Leaf 1 (attack-all): Score 98—optimal. Deal 2 unblocked damage (5→3 life), leaving opponent at critical life total; next turn I can finish with remaining Apes + spell. Leaf 2 & 3 (hold one Ape): Score 25 each—suboptimal. Opponent has no creatures to block or attack, so holding back sacrifices damage output without strategic benefit.

Declare Attackers resolved: both Kird Apes are now attacking (tapped). Pass priority to move to Declare Blockers phase. Opponent has no creatures, so no blocks are possible—combat damage will resolve uncontested.

Declare Blockers phase (opponent's decision): They have no creatures to block with. Pass priority; opponent will have no blocks to declare. Move to Combat Damage phase where 2 unblocked damage resolves.

Combat Damage phase: Combat damage has resolved (2 unblocked Ape damage dealt; opponent: 5 → 3 life). Pass priority to end combat. Opponent now at 3 life, critical position. Move to End Combat and then End Turn to complete my turn 9.
End Combat phase: Pass priority. My creatures will untap at the start of my next turn during the untap step. Proceed to End Turn and finish my turn 9. Opponent at 3 life, very close to losing.

Postcombat Main phase (turn 9): Pass priority. No need to cast Monstrous Rage—opponent is at 3 life, already critical. Next turn I attack with 2 untapped Kird Apes for 2 damage (3 → 1 life), then finish with spell or combat. End turn and proceed to opponent's turn 10.
End Turn (Cleanup): Pass priority. My turn 9 ends. Opponent proceeds to turn 10 at 3 life, facing lethal next turn when my Kird Apes untap and attack again.
Opponent's upkeep (turn 10): Pass priority. They're at 3 life facing lethal. Skip to my turn where I untap my Kird Apes and attack for the final 2 damage to win.

Opponent's Precombat Main phase (turn 10): They've cast a Nessian Courser (3/3 with summoning sickness). Pass priority; they can cast more spells or pass to combat. My Kird Apes will be untapped for my next turn to deliver lethal damage (opponent at 3 life, need 2 more damage).

Begin Combat (opponent's turn 10): Pass priority. Opponent's Nessian Courser has summoning sickness and cannot attack. They'll pass through combat with no attackers. Skip to my turn 11 where I untap and attack for lethal.
Cast Lightning Bolt targeting opponent player B. Deals 3 damage directly (3 life → 0 life). Opponent loses immediately. Game over—player A wins!
Target player B (opponent). Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage directly (3 life → 0 life). Opponent loses. Player A wins the game!

Precombat Main: Lightning Bolt has been cast and should resolve, dealing 3 damage to opponent (bringing them from 3 to 0 life). Game should end. Pass priority to conclude game state. Player A wins with superior tempo and burn sequencing.
